title: Galois-invariant closed subsets of a Galois base change descend
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $\bar k/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] that is Galois, i.e. separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and normal (for every $\alpha\in\bar k$ the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $k$ is a product of polynomials of degree one in $\bar k[T]$); it may be of infinite degree. Write $\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$ for the group of $k$-algebra automorphisms of $\bar k$. Let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] and $X_{\bar k}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ its base change [def-pc-base-change]. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$ let $\sigma_X=\mathrm{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma):X_{\bar k}\to X_{\bar k}$ be the base change of the $k$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma):\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; it is an automorphism of the scheme $X_{\bar k}$, and $(\sigma\circ\tau)_X=\tau_X\circ\sigma_X$. Let $p:X_{\bar k}\to X$ be the projection. Let $\bar T\subseteq X_{\bar k}$ be a closed subset such that $\sigma_X(\bar T)=\bar T$ for every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$. Then there is a closed subset $T\subseteq X$ with $p^{-1}(T)=\bar T$.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma Tag 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois, lines 898--934), with the action of equation (equation-galois-action-base-change-kbar), lines 850--874

proof.text: The automorphisms $\sigma_X$. Let $q:X_{\bar k}\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ be the second projection. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$, $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ is a morphism over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ since $\sigma$ is a $k$-algebra map, and by functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and of base change [def-pc-base-change] (uniqueness in the universal property of the fibre product) $(\sigma\circ\tau)_X=\tau_X\circ\sigma_X$ and $(\mathrm{id})_X=\mathrm{id}$; so $\sigma_X$ is an automorphism with inverse $(\sigma^{-1})_X$, in particular a bijection of the underlying set. By the definition of $\sigma_X=\mathrm{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ as an induced morphism of fibre products, $p\circ\sigma_X=p$ and $q\circ\sigma_X=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ q$. Since $\sigma_X$ is bijective and $\sigma_X(\bar T)=\bar T$, also $\sigma_X^{-1}(\bar T)=\bar T$. (This is the action (equation-galois-action-base-change-kbar); the same argument is step 0 of [lem-weil-pbc-galois-base-change-qc-open-descends], written out here.)

Affine charts of $X_{\bar k}$. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open and $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ an isomorphism onto the open subscheme $U$ [def-pc-scheme]; $A$ is a $k$-algebra through the composite $\operatorname{Spec}A\to U\subseteq X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a unique ring map $k\to A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put $\bar A=A\otimes_k\bar k$, $\iota_A:A\to\bar A$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, and $\iota_2:\bar k\to\bar A$, $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $V=U$, $W=Y=\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$) the canonical morphism $U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to X_{\bar k}$ is an open immersion with image $p^{-1}(U)$, compatible with the projections; by functoriality of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] $\iota_U$ induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\cong U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\cong\operatorname{Spec}\bar A$ with projections $\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_A)$, $\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_2)$. Composing, we get an open immersion $j:\operatorname{Spec}\bar A\to X_{\bar k}$, a homeomorphism onto the open $p^{-1}(U)$, with $p\circ j=\iota_U\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_A)$ and $q\circ j=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_2)$. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$ let $\varphi_\sigma=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\sigma:\bar A\to\bar A$, $a\otimes b\mapsto a\otimes\sigma(b)$: a ring homomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-map-ring-hom] (applied to $\sigma$ and $N=A$, through the symmetry $A\otimes_k\bar k\cong\bar k\otimes_kA$), with inverse $\varphi_{\sigma^{-1}}$, so a ring automorphism; $\varphi_\sigma\circ\iota_A=\iota_A$ and $\varphi_\sigma\circ\iota_2=\iota_2\circ\sigma$. Claim: $\sigma_X\circ j=j\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_\sigma)$. Both composites with $p$ equal $\iota_U\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_A)$ (left: $p\circ\sigma_X=p$ by step 0; right: $\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_A)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_\sigma)=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_\sigma\circ\iota_A)=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_A)$), and both composites with $q$ equal $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_2)=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_2\circ\sigma)$ (left: $q\circ\sigma_X=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ q$; right: $\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_2)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_\sigma)=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_\sigma\circ\iota_2)$); by the uniqueness in the universal property of $X_{\bar k}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ [def-pc-fibre-product] they are equal. In this chart $\sigma_X$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\sigma)$ and $p$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_A)$, which is the setting of Stacks' affine case $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois), proof, lines 911-934 ('This lemma immediately reduces to the case where X = Spec(A) is affine'); the chart is written out by the agent

proof.text: The radical ideal $\bar I$ and its invariance. $\bar T_U:=j^{-1}(\bar T)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}\bar A$ ($j$ is continuous), so $\bar T_U=V(J)$ for an ideal $J\subseteq\bar A$ by the definition of the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; $\bar I:=\sqrt J$ is a radical ideal with $V(\bar I)=V(J)=\bar T_U$, and it is the only radical ideal with this property [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq]. For a ring homomorphism $\varphi:R\to R'$ and an ideal $K\subseteq R$ one has $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)^{-1}(V(K))=V(\varphi(K)R')$, since $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)(\mathfrak q)=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $K\subseteq\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\iff\varphi(K)\subseteq\mathfrak q$ $(*)$. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$, by step 1 and step 0, $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_\sigma)^{-1}(\bar T_U)=(j\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_\sigma))^{-1}(\bar T)=(\sigma_X\circ j)^{-1}(\bar T)=j^{-1}(\sigma_X^{-1}(\bar T))=\bar T_U$, so by $(*)$ $V(\varphi_\sigma(\bar I))=V(\bar I)$ ($\varphi_\sigma(\bar I)$ is an ideal as $\varphi_\sigma$ is surjective). The image of a radical ideal under a ring automorphism is radical, so $\varphi_\sigma(\bar I)=\bar I$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq]. This is Stacks' 'Assumption (2) implies that $\sigma(\bar I)=\bar I$'.

A finite Galois subextension. Let $x\in\bar I$ and write $x=\sum_{i=1}^ma_i\otimes b_i$ with $a_i\in A$, $b_i\in\bar k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension] applied to $S=\{b_1,\dots,b_m\}$ there is a subfield $k\subseteq M\subseteq\bar k$ containing $S$ with $M/k$ finite Galois. Let $\psi=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes(M\hookrightarrow\bar k):A\otimes_kM\to\bar A$, a ring homomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-map-ring-hom], with $\psi(a\otimes1)=\iota_A(a)$; then $x=\psi(x')$ for $x'=\sum_ia_i\otimes b_i\in A\otimes_kM$. Let $G=\operatorname{Aut}(M/k)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] $G$ is finite, $d:=|G|=\dim_kM\ge1$, and its fixed field is $k$. For $\tau\in G$ let $\varphi'_\tau=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\tau$, a ring automorphism of $A\otimes_kM$ (as in step 1), with $\varphi'_\rho\circ\varphi'_\tau=\varphi'_{\rho\circ\tau}$ (check on $a\otimes y$).

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois), proof, lines 911-934, lines 914-916 ('There exists a finite Galois extension $k'/k$ contained in $\bar k$ such that $x\in A\otimes_kk'$. Set $G=\mathrm{Gal}(k'/k)$')

proof.text: The conjugates of $x$ lie in $\bar I$. Let $\tau\in G$. Since $\bar k/k$ and $M/k$ are normal, [lem-weil-pbc-normal-subextension-automorphism-extends] gives $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\bar k/k)$ with $\sigma|_M=\tau$. Then $\psi\circ\varphi'_\tau=\varphi_\sigma\circ\psi$ (both send $a\otimes y$ to $a\otimes\tau(y)=a\otimes\sigma(y)$, and both are additive), so $\psi(\varphi'_\tau(x'))=\varphi_\sigma(x)\in\varphi_\sigma(\bar I)=\bar I$ by step 2.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois), proof, lines 911-934 (implicit in 'Set $P(T)=\prod_{\sigma\in G}(T-\sigma(x))$': the elements of $\mathrm{Gal}(k'/k)$ are restrictions of elements of $\mathrm{Gal}(\bar k/k)$, Fields 0BME/0BMK)

proof.text: The polynomial $P$. Put $P(T)=\prod_{\tau\in G}(T-\varphi'_\tau(x'))=T^d+c_1T^{d-1}+\dots+c_d\in(A\otimes_kM)[T]$, monic of degree $d$, with $c_j=(-1)^je_j\big((\varphi'_\tau(x'))_{\tau\in G}\big)$, $e_j$ the $j$-th elementary symmetric polynomial. $P(x')=0$, the factor for $\tau=\mathrm{id}$ being $x'-x'$. For $\rho\in G$, applying the ring automorphism $\varphi'_\rho$ to the coefficients gives $\prod_\tau(T-\varphi'_{\rho\circ\tau}(x'))=P(T)$, since $\tau\mapsto\rho\circ\tau$ is a permutation of $G$; so $\varphi'_\rho(c_j)=c_j$ for all $\rho\in G$ and all $j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-field-extension-galois-invariants] (for $M/k$, the group $G$ with fixed field $k$, and the $k$-vector space $A$) there are unique $a_j\in A$ with $c_j=a_j\otimes1$. So $P\in A[T]$, Stacks' '$(A\otimes_kk')^G[T]=A[T]$ (by basic Galois theory)'.

$\bar I=\sqrt{I\bar A}$. Let $I=\iota_A^{-1}(\bar I)$, an ideal of $A$ ('$A\cap\bar I$'). $\psi(c_j)=\iota_A(a_j)$, and $\psi(c_j)=(-1)^je_j\big((\psi\varphi'_\tau(x'))_\tau\big)$ is a sum of products of $j\ge1$ elements of $\bar I$ (step 4), so lies in $\bar I$; hence $a_j\in I$. Applying $\psi$ to $P(x')=0$ gives $x^d=-\sum_{j=1}^d\iota_A(a_j)x^{d-j}\in I\bar A$ (the ideal of $\bar A$ generated by $\iota_A(I)$), so $x\in\sqrt{I\bar A}$. As $x\in\bar I$ was arbitrary, $\bar I\subseteq\sqrt{I\bar A}$. Conversely $\iota_A(I)\subseteq\bar I$ gives $I\bar A\subseteq\bar I$, and $\bar I$ is radical, so $\sqrt{I\bar A}\subseteq\bar I$. Hence $\bar I=\sqrt{I\bar A}$.

The affine case. By $(*)$ of step 2 for $\iota_A$, $\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_A)^{-1}(V(I))=V(I\bar A)$, and $V(I\bar A)=V(\sqrt{I\bar A})=V(\bar I)=\bar T_U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] and step 6. Let $T_U=\iota_U(V(I))$, a closed subset of $U$ ($V(I)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\iota_U$ is a homeomorphism onto $U$). By step 1, $j^{-1}(p^{-1}(T_U))=(p\circ j)^{-1}(T_U)=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_A)^{-1}(\iota_U^{-1}(T_U))=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_A)^{-1}(V(I))=\bar T_U=j^{-1}(\bar T)$. Since $p^{-1}(T_U)\subseteq p^{-1}(U)$ and $j$ is a bijection onto $p^{-1}(U)$, $p^{-1}(T_U)=\bar T\cap p^{-1}(U)$. (Stacks: 'setting $T=V(I)$ is a solution'.)

$p$ is surjective. $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ have one point each [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The projection $p:X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to X$ is its base change along $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change].

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 038B (lemma-closed-fixed-by-Galois), proof, lines 911-934 (used in the reduction to the affine case; written out by the agent)

proof.text: Reduction to the affine case (gluing). Put $T:=p(\bar T)\subseteq X$. For every affine open $U\subseteq X$, with $T_U$ as in step 7: since $p$ is surjective (step 8), $T_U=p(p^{-1}(T_U))=p(\bar T\cap p^{-1}(U))=p(\bar T)\cap U=T\cap U$. The affine opens cover $X$ [def-pc-scheme], and $T\cap U$ is closed in $U$ for each of them, so $X\setminus T=\bigcup_U(U\setminus(T\cap U))$ is open and $T$ is closed. Moreover $p^{-1}(T)\cap p^{-1}(U)=p^{-1}(T\cap U)=p^{-1}(T_U)=\bar T\cap p^{-1}(U)$ for every affine open $U$, and the $p^{-1}(U)$ cover $X_{\bar k}$, so $p^{-1}(T)=\bar T$.
